_comment: The Passwall Node claim for PSP major 4: the wire generation, the supported set, and the per-release review notes the panel shows in the upgrade dialog. IT REPLACED TWO FILES, and that is the point of the merge. This file used to be docs/compat/node-v4.json — the runtime manifest, which the CI planner and the compatibility matrix read by position at min_supported — while the DISPLAY metadata (notes, install methods, platforms, the published Docker tag) lived in a second, HAND-MAINTAINED file COMPILED INTO THE PANEL (internal/adapters/noderelease/reviewed.json). Adding a release therefore meant editing two documents and re-publishing the panel, because only one of them was fetched. THE TWO VOCABULARIES ARE NOT THE SAME AXIS AND BOTH REMAIN: released_nodes[].upgrade_methods (linux-systemd | managed-docker) is what the upgrade machinery and the verification profiles mean by a path, and released_nodes[].install_methods (linux | docker | manual) is what the operator picks in the dialog and is cross-checked against the published assets. THE RELEASE LIST IS AN ALLOW-LIST, NOT A RANGE: a reviewed release carries notes and platforms, which a min/max pair cannot hold, so this document names releases rather than bounding them. min_supported is a floor over the same list, matched BY POSITION in released_nodes — see min_supported_doc. THIS DOCUMENT IS DELIBERATELY SEPARATE from docs/compat/releases-v1.json (+ .sig): that one is the signed, opt-in ADMISSION policy, this one is the unsigned runtime manifest a default install fetches, and folding them together would put a signature over a document that must work without a key.
min_supported_doc: The OLDEST Passwall-Node version this panel still tests. Everything from this row onward in released_nodes is the supported set, and that set is exactly what the released-range CI matrix exercises. MATCHED BY POSITION IN released_nodes, NOT by a version comparison. The positional rule was introduced because the legacy scheme's dotless prereleases sorted wrongly as text ('v0.0.1-beta9' above 'v0.0.1-beta11'), so comparing the strings would have silently inverted the floor. THAT REASON IS GONE - a version is three integers now, and integers compare correctly - and the mechanism stays because it is the one both sides already implement: the planner slices this list by indexOf exactly as this field is read. THIS SELECTS WHAT IS TESTED, NOT WHAT MAY CONNECT. No production code reads this field -- only the two workflows and the matrix test do -- so raising it stops testing the versions below it and does nothing else: an older node keeps syncing, and nothing refuses it for sitting below this row. Refusing a node is a separate decision about the wire generation (see wire.min_protocol_version) and needs its own change, announcement and migration acceptance; a floor move must not do that work by implication. Raising it is still BREAKING in the sense that matters here: every version below it stops being tested, so a regression in one of them stops being caught. Record it in docs/compat-policy.md's history, naming what is now untested. The field exists so the matrix can stop growing -- without a floor every release adds a permanent row.

released_nodes.notes: Reviewed PSP v4 agent protocol and exact release packaging. The first release under the product scheme: the tag is release/4.0.0 and the version is 4.0.0, the archive is named passwall-node_4.0.0_linux_<arch>.tar.gz, and the exact image tag is 4.0.0. The download chain was verified against the published release rather than constructed: the slash-bearing URL serves the asset, the checksum manifest names it exactly once, and sha256sum --check passes. State schema 9 and upgrade contract 1 are unchanged. Published as a pre-release, so no stable pointer moved. Remote upgrades require Linux/systemd, the upgrade helper, and unchanged state schema 9. Docker uses container-managed updates. Docker and Windows end-to-end installation has not been verified, and no end-to-end upgrade on a real host has been performed for this release.
